notes: readOnly means "cannot broadcast a transaction". A readOnly command may still have sideEffects — ipfs-pin(--pin) publishes publicly and irreversibly when --pin is passed.
destructive commands require an explicit --yes (or POP_ASSUME_YES=1) in every non-interactive context; --json is never consent.
POP_READONLY=1 makes the process structurally unable to sign or pin. POP_ADDRESS/--address serves identity-scoped reads without a key.
The agent runtime commands (pop agent, pop brain) live in @poa-box/agent and are not covered here.

When set, the tool calls name() on the target before probing and warns (non-fatal) if the result doesn't match. commands.description: Check whether a domain/address is invited and can still claim

proof.description: Also emit the merkle proof for this entry

commands.name: zkemail claims
commands.description: Who has claimed a role via a ZK Email invite

limit.description: Maximum claims to show (most recent first)

commands.name: zkemail build-allowlist
commands.description: Compute an allowlist doc + merkle root, optionally pin to IPFS

domain.description: Invite a whole domain, e.g. --domain anthropic.com (repeatable)

email.description: Invite a specific address, e.g. --email alice@org.com (repeatable)

file.description: JSON file of allowlist entries (or an existing allowlist doc to re-publish)

hat.description: Hat ID(s) granted to every --domain/--email entry (repeatable)

out.description: Write the allowlist JSON to this path

pin.description: Pin the allowlist to IPFS (otherwise compute locally only)

commands.name: zkemail propose-allowlist
commands.description: Propose committing an allowlist root + CID (executor-gated)

cid.description: IPFS CIDv0 of the pinned allowlist file

root.description: Merkle root from pop zkemail build-allowlist

skip-verify.description: Skip fetching the pinned file to confirm it reproduces --root (not recommended)

commands.name: config show
commands.description: Show active configuration

commands.name: config validate
commands.description: Test RPC and subgraph connectivity

commands.name: mcp serve
commands.description: Serve the CLI as an MCP (Model Context Protocol) stdio server

allow-destructive.description: Also expose destructive writes — implies --allow-writes (or POP_MCP_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=1)

allow-writes.description: Expose non-destructive write commands as tools (or POP_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES=1)

commands.name: init
commands.description: Interactive setup: wallet, chain, default org, .env

chain.description: Chain ID to configure (100 Gnosis, 42161 Arbitrum, 11155111 Sepolia, 84532 Base Sepolia)

generate-key.description: Generate a fresh wallet non-interactively (prints the mnemonic once)

org.description: Default org name or hex ID (POP_DEFAULT_ORG)
